Claude Code usage report: 29 Sep to 13 Oct 2026

Summary: Opus 5.5 at long context accounts for almost all of the usage. 75% of the cost comes from re-reading cached context.
Totals: 334 sessions, 99,301 API calls, 26.2B tokens read from cache.

What's consuming it, biggest first
1. Long sessions. Every call re-reads the whole conversation, and the average context was about 264K tokens. Calls made with more than 300K of context account for 59% of all input tokens. The top 15 sessions are about 46% of the total. The biggest single session was 04957a5e (sofar): 5,472 calls, 6.6% on its own.
2. Many small Bash calls. 81,775 Bash calls, 82% of all tool calls. Largest groups: sed -n (12.7K), grep (about 14K), python3 - (7.3K). Each one re-reads the full context, so a 20-line sed -n costs about 260K tokens. The Read tool was used only 2,432 times.
3. Subagents: 41% of cost. 51.9K calls. They wrote more to the cache than the main sessions did (216M vs 209M tokens) but produced only 4.1M output tokens, against 34.2M for the main sessions.
4. Model: Opus 5.5 is 98.7% of the cost. Sonnet, Haiku and Fable together are about 1.3%.
5. Effort level: xhigh 39.5%, medium 48.8%, high 11.7%.

Breakdown (share of cost)
- By project: splen 72.7%, sofar plus its worktrees 23.5%, memory-lab 3.4%
- By token type: cache reads 74.9%, cache writes 19.6%, output 5.5%
- By day: 10-13 Oct is 50% of the two weeks. 10 Oct alone is 17.3% (19.8K calls).

How to bring it down
- Run /compact or /clear before a session passes about 250K tokens of context.
- Use one Read call or one combined script instead of chains of sed -n and grep.
- Use Sonnet or Haiku for read-only search subagents, and run fewer agents in parallel.
- Keep xhigh effort for hard problems only.

Note: costs are weighted in Opus-input-token equivalents, not dollars: cache read 0.1x, 5-minute cache write 1.25x, 1-hour cache write 2x, output 5x. Because nearly everything ran on Opus 5.5, the percentage shares should still hold.
